plan: My private value is $34. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $34 ensures I only win if the item is truly worth more to me than others. If I win, I'll pay less than my bid. If I bid too low, I risk losing an item that provides me net positive value. With no prior round history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid is most rational.

My private value is $28. My optimal strategy is to bid strategically to maximize potential profit. Since the third-highest bid determines my payment if I win, I want to bid slightly above my value but not excessively. Given the random nature of other bidders' values, a bid around $30-$35 seems reasonable. This allows some buffer above my value while not overcommitting. I'll aim to capture potential profit by bidding just above my true value.
